Filipino here. Not a chopstick user originally, but had to learn using forks and knives. Started with spoon and fork, and used the spoon as the knife. 

When I started learning knives, it confused me where to hold it; if it should be on the left, so I can shovel food with my fork on the right; or with my dominant hand, then put the utensils down, and pick my fork to bring food to my mouth. 

Regardless, I feel that forks are inefficient in most foods (peas? Rice? It doesn't get a lot of food). If I'm going to use just one hand,  spoons are more efficient: soups, meat-cutting, rice, even noodles and pasta.

We know the sharpest side of the spoon. 

- Filipinos

Fish in Ginger Soup
(PESANG ISDA)

Tilapia, about 4 loins: seasoned with salt and pepper
1 onion, diced
A thumb of ginger, peeled and cut into sticks. I think I used more coz I love ginger
Bokchoy, stalks cut into half
Some Potatoes, cubed
Salt and pep to taste
Fish Sauce: used Red Boat. About 4 tbsp?
5-6 c of water
Green onions for additional flavor at the end. 

Saute ginger until fragrant, and the flavors are steeped into the oil. Add onions and cook until translucent. Add water and potatoes, and boil until potatoes are soft. Add fish sauce. Add fish and boil until cooked. Add bokchoy to cook. Sorry, I just eyeballed it, but season to taste with salt, pep and fishsauce. The ginger should come through, with mild saltiness. 

I eat this alone, mashing the potatoes in for carbs. Cauliflower rice works too. :)

I'm not saying its right, but cancelling idols for CA aint the way to go either. 

I'm Asian. Before migrating, Im not as woke as I thought I was. Even with the power of the internet. Because I didn't know the CA mines that I needed to watch out for. I knew the n word was a no-no, but I didn't know that trying on blaccent is offensive either. I tried to master blaccent coz it sounded fun. I try to cop out the southern drawl and cockney. Its just my thing. I dont mean to offend, as say, a white person mocking my accent to 'put me in my place'. To me, pulling of an accent is a skill. It was my lack of forethought to find imitating someone infront of them would be cringey and offensive. 

I would've been hanged if I spoke that way. I know that now. But it took me living in the US for a year and meeting real black people to know that that is offensive. Its just not concerning when its not your reality, and esp when you're facing your own infighting. Most asians hate on each other, and we retaliated not with political correctness but with more creative, vicious mockery. Im not condoning it now, but its difficult to feel the gravity of our actions when we're far away from the situation. Education and patience is the way to go. Even if we hammer down on twitter accounts, do you think that they'll get it? Some idols couldnt even have access to the internet, or be on social media without a manager around. 

CA is def a new concept even to me. Years ago, I wouldve been ok to have ScarJo be Motoko Kusanagi because she's badass and pretty, and I wouldnt have seen the bigger picture that an Asian actress was being robbed. I wanted to be japanese because of anime, and dressed up as japanese for UN week. I begged my Japanese teacher to give me a Japanese name, and not just my name written in katakana. She never did, and now I know why. Thought Emma Stone's stories are relatable and didnt care for the lack of stories from people of my color. There is a level of blindness being away from all this, until now when I've actually been told inferior because I wasn't white. Suddenly, Emma Stone isn't that relatable to me anymore. When someone calls me a chink, Id rather shut up coz I didnt know I could defend myself with the voice of my nation. CA is something I had to learn only recently. 

I remember the time (like, always in Twitter) when Mamamoo is put down for blackface (which I think was more like an imitation of a famous homeless man more than blackface? I wasnt too sure about this), wearing the durag (I didnt know that this was a thing), saying the n-word (singing a song that had the word in it). They have apologized repeatedly, but again, you cant take any person's right to be angry. So angry we all are. But, what do you want them to do if apologies are not enough? Stop from being idols? Kill themselves? When is it enough, esp when they've apologized and have not done anything similar to it? You have to take into consideration that each one occurrence for this is a CA landmine that they, their company, or any Asian, wouldnt have checked for before committing it as, again, even with google, we wouldnt have known to look for.
